title: Enchanted Scroll Fragments
description:
In an ancient library, a magical scroll `s` has been torn into individual character fragments. Each character keeps its original position as a unique **ID** (1-based).

You must process a series of mystical queries that can:
- Check if two fragments are still part of the same scroll piece.
- Extract specific letters into new scroll pieces.
- Merge scroll pieces (earlier created piece absorbs the later one).
- Report the letter composition of all existing scroll pieces at the end.

Return the array `result` containing all answers from type 1 and type 5 queries.

**Note:** Expected time complexity should be efficient (better than O(q * n)).

examples.explanation: After processing all queries, the result array contains the outputs from check and final composition queries.
Characters are moved and merged according to the rules, and the final composition is reported.

constraints:
- 1 ≤ |s| ≤ 100000
- 1 ≤ |queries| ≤ 200000
- 1 ≤ x, y ≤ |s|
- For type 3 queries, x ≤ y
- 1 ≤ |word| ≤ 26
- All characters in `s` and `word` are lowercase English letters
- Expected overall time complexity: efficient handling of unions and frequency tracking

hints.content: Each fragment belongs to a group. You'll need a way to track which group each character ID currently belongs to.
Pattern: Union-Find (Disjoint Set Union) with path compression and union by rank will be very useful for managing groups.

BEGIN Track Groups
    Use Union-Find to manage which characters belong to the same scroll piece.
    Maintain frequency count for each group.
    When moving letters (queries 2 & 3), create new groups and update frequencies.
    For merge (query 4), link the newer group to the older one.
    For query 5, traverse groups in creation order and build composition strings.
END
